newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN CABINET APPROVES FIVE-DAY WORK WEEK.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN CABINET APPROVES FIVE-DAY WORK WEEK.

text.p: Taiwan's cabinet has approved a proposal to begin a five-day work week, giving public servants two days off every second and fourth weeks of each month effective from January 1998, officials said on Wednesday.

"The programme was approved under the condition that the public would not receive less quality service from public servants," an official quoted government spokesman David Lee as telling reporters on Tuesday.
The private sector will not be forced to follow suit, but it will have the option of doing so, the official said.
Business executives have long opposed the programme when it was discussed and initiated months ago, saying it would hurt Taiwan's competitiveness in the international market.
Public servants now have to work six days a week.
Officials said the new policy would not reduce government agencies' work hours because public servants would no longer have days off for eight national holidays.

Taiwan's stock, bond, money and foreign exchange markets would follow the programme to close on every second and fourth Saturday of the month, but open on the said eight national holidays, officials said.
Officials declined to give a timetable for implementing an overall five-day work week.
